title: Problem awareness — inside a GLP-1 gut

beats.text: This is what's happening inside your gut on a GLP-1, and it causes your appetite to slow down, and suddenly going to the bathroom gets harder.
beats.visual: Translucent character stops mid-bite with a sharp expression of discomfort as the interior stomach becomes visible; movement already underway in frame one. No swelling into obstruction.
beats.why: Preserve the user's exact hook. The appetite/bathroom contradiction creates immediate recognition while the anatomical view promises an explanation.

beats.text: Watch the stomach. Food moves through it with muscular contractions. A GLP-1 can slow how quickly that food leaves. See how it stays there longer instead of passing through at the same pace?
beats.visual: Side-on illustrative stomach follows food through continued contractions and a slower exit. Hold one legible action; label illustration. No precise retention time shown.
beats.why: Uses deictic language to direct attention to a changing process rather than merely naming an organ. Does not imply full gastric paralysis.

beats.text: You feel full for longer. And when constipation becomes part of the picture, you want more than a smaller appetite. You want digestion to feel comfortable again.
beats.visual: New dining-room wide view: character sets plate aside, shifts uncomfortably and looks toward an interrupted daily activity. No promised post-product result.
beats.why: Turns the mechanism into an everyday cost and a specific desire before introducing a solution. Constipation is not declared to have one universal cause.

beats.text: First, celery juice powder, which contains a plant compound called apigenin. [E1: Explain its supported digestive action and how that addresses the problem just shown.]
beats.visual: Celery ingredient macro, then reserve a distinct stomach-wall demonstration ONLY if matching action is supported. No brand or packaging.
beats.why: The first ingredient must earn its place through an action tied to the problem; an ingredient name alone is incomplete.

beats.text: Second, chlorophyllin, a derivative of the green pigment in plants. [E2: Explain its supported action on the relevant gas, bloating or odor symptom, and why it complements the first ingredient.]
beats.visual: Separate green pigment macro; reserve a distinct relevant mechanism view pending E2. Do not animate disappearing bubbles by default.
beats.why: The second role must add a specific contribution to the same problem. Identity or green coloration cannot stand in for evidence of that contribution.

beats.text: Third, prebiotic fiber. Watch it reach the large intestine, where beneficial bacteria use it as food.
beats.visual: Labeled FOS particles travel to a colon microenvironment and are used by resident microbes. No stomach-emptying acceleration.
beats.why: Demonstrate the supported prebiotic function at the correct location; preserve its distinction from the preceding unverified roles.

beats.text: [E3: Connect those three actions to one supported combined benefit that answers the opening problem.]
beats.visual: Three previously taught role labels remain on screen and connect to one benefit ONLY once E1/E2/E3 have factual wording. No product yet.
beats.why: This is the logical payoff of the UMS. Product cannot enter while the viewer is still waiting to learn why the ingredients belong together.

beats.text: Motilli combines those three ingredients in two daily gummies: celery juice powder, chlorophyllin and prebiotic fiber.
beats.visual: First product/package/brand reveal at 'Motilli', strictly after completed combined-benefit sentence. Accurate bottle and two heart-shaped gummies.
beats.why: The product is positioned as the concrete formula only after the viewer understands all roles. This passage remains conditional on resolving the UMS, not proof of it.

beats.text: Take them as directed with water. No separate ingredients to measure or mix. Tap to shop Motilli, backed by a 90-day money-back guarantee.
beats.visual: New countertop routine action with water followed by Shop Motilli/guarantee graphic. No medical before/after montage.
beats.why: Convenience belongs after mechanism and product selection; the CTA makes the actual next action clear.

beats.visual: Hold package and readable CTA, music resolves.
beats.why: Three seconds to read and act; not extra efficacy messaging.

beats.text: This is what happens when you take MiraLAX or bulking fiber for constipation on a GLP-1. Watch where each one works.
beats.visual: Split view with PEG-associated stool hydration on one side and psyllium gel hydration on the other; both actions begin immediately.
beats.why: Directly pays off the comparison promise with distinct visible processes. Neither side is depicted as inevitably failing.

beats.text: Here, MiraLAX holds water in your stool, helping it soften and pass. Over here, a bulking fiber like psyllium absorbs water and helps form stool. Both can help you go.
beats.visual: Remain in split demonstration; highlight PEG on 'Here' then psyllium on 'Over here'. Continuous narration; no unnecessary base-shot cut.
beats.why: The language guides the viewer through a real distinction and preserves the treatments' supported usefulness.

beats.text: Now look higher up. A GLP-1 can slow food leaving the stomach. Softening stool doesn't necessarily change that. If you're still full and uncomfortable between bowel movements, you want to understand that part of the picture, too.
beats.visual: Spatial move to a separate stomach view, then distinct character shot after a small meal. No implication that colon and stomach are one plug of waste.
beats.why: Builds the canonical spatial contrast without asserting that constipation remedies are useless. Unresolved discomfort creates a reason for the subsequent explanation.

beats.text: This is what happens when you take celery, chlorophyll, and fiber every day while you're constipated on a GLP-1.
beats.visual: Three clearly labeled ingredient streams move toward a translucent digestive map while the character reacts sharply to discomfort. No beneficial effect or product shown in opening.
beats.why: Uses the user's requested outcome-demonstration framework and names the unbranded ingredients. The promised outcome depends on completing the evidence slots.

beats.text: But first, look at the gut they're going into. Food moves through the stomach with muscular contractions. A GLP-1 can slow how quickly it leaves, so you feel full for longer.
beats.visual: Move from ingredient recognition to side-on stomach; show continued contractions and slower exit. Distinct composition from A's camera for concept variety.
beats.why: Establishes the problem before teaching ingredients so their roles have a purpose; avoids launching into an ingredient list without a viewer need.

beats.text: When constipation comes with that, the question becomes: what does each ingredient actually do, and why would you take them together? Let's follow them.
beats.visual: Character pauses a daily activity with discomfort; camera transitions to three neutral numbered ingredient areas without brand.
beats.why: States the exact question the UMS must answer. It creates desire for a relevant explanation rather than a generic mixing convenience pitch.
